key_insight: NH4SCN promotes high-n quasi-2D perovskite scaffolds that template highly (110)-ordered 3D MAPbI3, rather than primarily improving transport through vertically oriented 2D layers.
engineering_relevance: Additive-controlled crystallization offers a route to better-ordered perovskite absorbers when quasi-2D scaffold kinetics and lattice matching are favorable.
method: Use spectroscopy and structural analysis to investigate NH4SCN-mediated crystallization.
Extend the nucleation window to suppress n = 1 phases and promote high-n quasi-2D scaffolds.
Assess lattice matching and cation dependence of scaffold-templated MAPbI3 growth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports structural evidence of highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3 and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, but provides no numerical device-performance results.
watch_item: The templating effect is cation dependent and requires both compatible lattices and successful kinetic control, limiting direct transfer to other formulations.
paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
